summary: Beatrice Municipal Airport (BIE) is a small general aviation facility serving the city of Beatrice in southeastern Nebraska. Operated by the municipality, it supports private aviation, flight training, and recreational flying for the local community and surrounding Gage County area. The airport features a single primary runway and serves as a convenient gateway for visitors to this historic Nebraska town, known for its heritage as the first capital of the Nebraska Territory.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Beatrice Municipal?
A: It is a small, publicly owned municipal airport primarily serving general aviation, private pilots, and flight training operations. Commercial passenger service is not available.

Q: Does Beatrice Municipal Airport have an air traffic control tower?
A: No, it is an uncontrolled airport. Pilots communicate on the common traffic advisory frequency (CTAF) and use visual flight rules procedures.

Q: How many runways does the airport have?
A: The airport features a single primary asphalt runway designated 14/32, suitable for small to mid-size general aviation aircraft.

Q: Are fuel services available at the airport?
A: Fuel services may be available during published hours, but pilots are advised to check current availability and contact the airport manager in advance for after-hours arrangements.
transport_tips: Since Beatrice Municipal Airport is a small general aviation facility, travelers typically arrange ground transportation in advance. Rental cars and local taxi services are the primary options for reaching the town of Beatrice, located just a few miles from the airport. Having a personal vehicle is the most convenient way to access the airport and surrounding areas.
local_tip: Frequent visitors should call the airport manager ahead of arrival, as the unattended nature of the field means hangar access, fueling, and ground services are often by appointment—coordinating in advance saves significant time during your visit.
